questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD mastery: per-namespace isolation, InitContainer usage, secret/config management, and production-grade guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for model pull from Secret
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for runtime parameters
- Probes and HPA for reliability and scale
- Idempotent DB writes to achieve at-least-once delivery
- NetworkPolicy to enforce namespace boundaries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ns-image-resize
  namespace: <ns>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-resize
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-model
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "download-model.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: model
              mountPath: /models
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry/ns-image-resize:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - secretRef: { name: resize-secret }
      volumes:
        - name: model
          emptyDir: {}
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 100
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchLabels:
                    app: image-resize
                topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
  ```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor idempotency and retry behavior?
- What changes if Kafka offset management moves to a separate transactional store?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Explores practical CKAD competencies: deployment orchestration, config/secret management, volumes, autoscaling, service exposure, and network isolation.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap/Secret, HPA
- ClusterIP service semantics
- NetworkPolicy gating and its limitations

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-app:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: my-app-config
        - secretRef:
            name: my-app-creds
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-pvc
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data-pvc
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
  storageClassName: standard
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: my-app-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: my-app
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 60
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  selector:
    app: my-app
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-api
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.0/24
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this in a cluster with a restricted CNI?
- What changes if the app becomes stateful or requires dynamic PVC provisioning?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical CKAD skills: using Kubernetes CSR API, namespace-scoped Secrets, and security controls in a rotation workflow.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes CertificateSigningRequest, automated approval, private CA
- Secrets and Secret Mounts, TLS configuration in Pods
- InitContainers and container probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting CA access
- RBAC implications and audit considerations

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob skeleton that triggers TLS rotation
# (Note: actual CSR creation is performed by a script in the container)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: tls-rotate
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: tls-rotate-sa
          containers:
          - name: rotate
            image: bitnami/kubectl
            command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl certificate approve csr-service-tls-rotation"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-service
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myservice:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: my-service-tls
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD workflow patterns: CronJobs, batch processing, and secret management within a namespace; validates knowledge of init containers, sidecars, and network hardening.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling in a namespace
- InitContainer dependency installation
- ConfigMap for BATCH_SIZE
- Secret for API credentials
- Sidecar for TLS cert rotation
- NetworkPolicy for internal egress controls
- Probes for readiness and liveness
- Idempotency vs at-least-once semantics

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: csv-ingest
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-csvkit
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'pip install csvkit && cp -r /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/* /shared/']
            volumeMounts:
            - name: shared-libs
              mountPath: /shared
          containers:
          - name: csv-processor
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'python /app/process.py']
            env:
            - name: BATCH_SIZE
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: app-config
                  key: BATCH_SIZE
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-credentials
                  key: token
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data-pvc
              mountPath: /data
            - name: shared-libs
              mountPath: /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
          - name: cert-rotator
            image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator
            volumeMounts:
            - name: certs
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs
          volumes:
          - name: data-pvc
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: data-pvc
          - name: shared-libs
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: certs
            emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-config
data:
  BATCH_SIZE: "10"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-credentials
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: csv-ingest-netpol
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: csv-ingest
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: data-portal
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **CronJob vs Deployment**: CronJobs provide scheduled execution but lack continuous availability; Deployments offer always-on processing but require custom scheduling logic.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing dependencies at runtime increases startup time vs pre-built images, but provides flexibility for version updates.
- **Sidecar complexity**: TLS cert rotation adds operational overhead but ensures security compliance; alternative is using cert-manager injection.
- **Batch processing**: Larger batches improve throughput but increase memory usage and failure impact; smaller batches provide better isolation but higher API call frequency.
- **NetworkPolicy scope**: Namespace-scoped policies provide good isolation but require per-namespace management; cluster-wide policies simplify administration but reduce granular control.
- **Storage patterns**: PVC-backed storage ensures data persistence across pod restarts but requires careful volume management; temporary storage simplifies cleanup but risks data loss during failures.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design production-ready batch workloads in Kubernetes, including secure configuration management, job lifecycle controls, and deployment strategies for config-driven restarts.

## Key Concepts
- **concurrencyPolicy: Forbid** - Prevents overlapping job executions, ensuring data consistency
- **backoffLimit: 3** - Limits retry attempts for failed pods before marking the job as failed
- **ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400** - Auto-cleansup completed jobs after 24 hours
- **successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3** - Retains recent successful job history for debugging/auditing
- **checksum annotation** - Triggers pod recreation when ConfigMap/Secret changes (requires script to generate hash)
- **envFrom** - Mounts all ConfigMap/Secret values as environment variables without explicit key mapping

## Verification Under Simulated Load
1. **Test concurrency**: Trigger manual job while another runs - should fail with "Cannot determine if job needs to be started"
2. **Test failure handling**: Set invalid config, verify backoff retries 3 times
3. **Test cleanup**: Check completed jobs are removed after 24h TTL

## Verification On Config Change
1. Update ConfigMap: `kubectl apply -f analytics-config.yaml`
2. Verify annotation checksum updates in next job
3. Confirm new pod picks up new environment variables
4. Use `kubectl get pods` to verify new pod creation timestamp

## Why This Is Asked
This question validates understanding of per-namespace resource governance in Kubernetes. It tests knowledge of how LimitRange and ResourceQuota work together to control pod sizing and cluster resource allocation.

## Key Concepts
- **LimitRange**: Sets default requests/limits applied to Pods that don't specify resources
- **ResourceQuota**: Enforces hard limits on total namespace resource consumption
- **Policy alignment**: Ensuring Deployments specify resources matching namespace defaults
- **Verification**: Testing policy enforcement with intentional over-allocation
- **Rollback**: Strategy for removing or scaling back resources when policies need adjustment

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: analytics-lr
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    default:
      cpu: "200m"
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: "100m"
      memory: 128Mi
```
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: analytics-quo
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  hard:
    cpu: "400m"
    memory: 512Mi
    requests.storage: "1Gi"
```
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: reporter
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reporter
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
```
## Verification Commands
```bash
kubectl apply -f limitrange.yaml
kubectl apply -f quota.yaml
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
kubectl describe resourcequota analytics-quo -n analytics
kubectl run overload-test --image=busybox --restart=Never --requests=cpu=500m,memory=600Mi --dry-run=server
```
## Rollback Strategy
```bash
kubectl delete -f quota.yaml
kubectl delete -f limitrange.yaml
kubectl scale deployment reporter --replicas=0 -n analytics
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to perform zero-downtime upgrades in a CKAD-like scenario with real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment strategy: RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable and maxSurge
- Graceful shutdown via PreStop lifecycle hook
- PodDisruptionBudget to protect minimum availability

## Code Example
```yaml
# Deployment patch focusing on zero-downtime upgrade
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: orders-api
  namespace: prod
spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: "0"
      maxSurge: "1"
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: orders-api
        image: orders-api:1.2
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/app/graceful-stop.sh"]
```
```yaml
# PodDisruptionBudget to allow maintenance without dropping below 2 pods
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: orders-api-pdb
  namespace: prod
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-api
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests your ability to design an isolated audit pattern with in-cluster API access, RBAC scoping, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control
- In-cluster API access using Secrets and ConfigMaps
- PVC-backed persistent logs and InitContainers for tooling
- NetworkPolicy for egress control to restrict traffic to the collector
- Health checks (readiness/liveness probes) for reliability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-baseline
  namespace: example
data:
  baseline.json: |
    {"pods": [], "services": []}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-auth
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: " collector-auth-token"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:
        - name: COLLECTOR_URL
          value: "http://collector.audit-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```bash
#!/bin/bash
endpoints=$(cat /etc/metrics/endpoints)	token=$(cat /secrets/metrics-token/token)
while true; do
  for ep in $endpoints; do
    status=$(curl -sI -w '%{http_code}' -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" "$ep")
    if [ "$status" != "200" ]; then echo "$ep failed: $status" >> /logs/metrics/summary.log; fi
  done
  sleep 300
done
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale and test this in a real cluster?
- What are risks with mounting Secrets in /secrets and how to mitigate?
